Guidance & outlook: There has been a marginal correction in price, which we, like I said , anticipated about 3% increase in raw material prices.
We had given a guidance that we will go to 18% by 2031.
Okay, so the journey from say 15, 16% EBITDA margin towards your target of 20%, some part would be operating leverage on the current base.
Growth & demand: We grew by about 23% and after that 7% was exchange related.
Europe, we grew by 21% and Australia, 7%, I mean, sorry 17%.
And if it is so volume driven, that is more than 20% growth in terms of volume growth has been there.
Margins & costs: We had a contribution - negative primarily because of raw material cost increases, tariffs, and product mix.
We started off the year thinking that there will be a 3% to 4% increase in material cost, cost by commodity, metal commodity prices, but in reality it was 5%.
What really happened is 5% to 6% is the increase in the raw material cost.
Capex & expansion: The same thing with other expenses, there's a 12% increase primarily because we have gone and taken on some rental premises for our motor plant, as well as, you know, what we sold, the facilities that we sold in the US, we have moved into rental facilities.
Our CAPEX, one is our MK2, which is our program for shifting our campus to the new campus from our city factory.
That's been about half of the CAPEX is towards that.
Balance sheet & cash: Net cash position in the company continues to be very strong.
Some part of it, clearly operating leverage, which is linked again to new products because they contribute to giving us the top line, right, by market share or growth into new markets.
At 3 levels, we will be looking at improving our EBITDA margin, not just relying on only leverage.
Risks & challenges: We've had some challenges in our service business in our distribution of operations.
Market is big, but there are still challenges for an Indian brand in that market.
So, the real challenge is not giving value propositions just to the end user but look at what is the unique value proposition that we give to distributors.

Guidance & outlook: On behalf of Asian Markets, we welcome you all to the Q4 and FY 25-26 earnings webinar of Elgi Equipments Limited.
I'll tell a little bit about what we expect for this year.
We are comfortable until June, and we are taking stock of what could be the scenarios going forward.
Growth & demand: Our sales grew by about 12%, contribution got impacted due to product mix and a little bit by tariffs.
Like I said, our revenue grew by 12% and our PBT grew by 17%.
Overall increase, I would say the volume growth across multiple verticals on average was around 3 to 4 percent, right.
Margins & costs: But during the year, because of the variation in tariffs starting from 10% to 50% inventory at various levels, we had this marginal impact.

In the employee cost, there's been a 16% increase, primarily because both in the US and in Europe, we have been reorganizing to bring some of the processes back to India like we are creating a shared service organization, we are investing into it.
We continue to generate 100% of the EBITDA as cash, even normalizing for extraordinary cash inflow like sale of property.
Capex & expansion: So part of it is our investment in our go to market that we had in India, which was sharpened there and some investments in IT, primarily our PLM investment.
So, when your capacity goes up in a factory, you're increasing your capacity, you need more compressed air to support that additional capacity.
Besides that, we will probably have a normal you know, balancing CapEx of around 70 crores.
Balance sheet & cash: Moving on to our net cash position, it continues to be pretty solid.
Risks & challenges: I will talk about specific challenges after I complete this presentation.
So that uncertainty is causing a little bit of an issue.

Guidance & outlook: In FY26, it's expected to be around 23 billion dollar and market is growing at 3.5% CAGR.
So, in terms of revenue, in FY21 we set a target for ourselves at USD 450 mn and we had considered a growth rate of 10% CAGR.
In terms of EBITDA margin, against a target of 16%, we'll close at 15% and in terms of return on capital employed, against a target of 30%, we'll close at 35%.
Growth & demand: So, the combination of all the segments will result in about 11% growth for us in this ﬁscal.
It's a combination of share of growth, share of market share growth, share of new products, share of new segments in existing products as well as new geographies.
Point number two is we are saying 4% growth India, 12% growth ELGI.
Margins & costs: This also means that we had considered a proﬁtability, so EBITDA margin of 16% and return on capital of 30%.
This USD 750 mn would be at 18% of EBITDA margin and around 35% of return on capital employed.
Let us say you said product margins are lower, aftermarket margins are higher, if not the exact numbers, but just the diƯerence between the product margins and the aftermarket margins.
Capex & expansion: So, at a point at which the tariƯs were upwards of 50 percent, customers in segments like textiles weren't necessarily keen on upgrading or investing in new capacity.
Interestingly, we have also seen that in spite of CAPEX, our CAPEX cycle has now started to come into play.

We can see a good amount of shift towards the Indian markets, I think there was 13% CAGR which we are targeting versus 10% in the previous ﬁve year block and so just wanted to understand and also the 200 bps margin expansion which we are building in for next ﬁve years.
Balance sheet & cash: As a result of this, the fact that we've generated more cash in our overseas subsidiaries, helped us pare down some of our loans and with the help of better working capital management, we also kind of reduced our working capital levels.
Again, the last couple of years very strong focus on working capital.
Net working capital, we have not added working capital in spite of growing our top line by 11%.
Risks & challenges: Foundry, motor production, our own pressure vessel and some of the machining that we do and the machines that we build for ourselves.
